snippet.title: Why is downtown Lisbon a grid? (1755 earthquake)
snippet.description:
Downtown Lisbon looks like graph paper, and that's because of one terrible morning: 1 November 1755. An earthquake, then a tsunami, then days of fire wiped out the old Baixa.

The part that gets me is what they did next. Instead of rebuilding the old tangle of alleys, they drew straight streets between two big squares, and hid a flexible wooden cage (the "gaiola") inside the walls so the next quake wouldn't bring everything down. The royal palace square, Terreiro do Paço, came back as Praça do Comércio: Commerce Square.

Have you been to Rua Augusta? Did the grid ever strike you as odd for such an old city?
